name: Learn: Storage
description: Master Kubernetes storage step by step — StorageClasses, PersistentVolumes, static PVC binding, mounting a volume in a pod, and setting a default StorageClass.
objective: CKA › Storage (10%). Goal: define StorageClasses, static PVs and PVCs, binding and mounting, and the default-class annotation.

questions.title: StorageClass
questions.teach:
A **StorageClass** describes a *kind* of storage and how dynamic volumes are provisioned.

**Key fields**
- `provisioner` — the driver that creates volumes (a CSI driver, `kubernetes.io/no-provisioner` for static-only local volumes, or here `rancher.io/local-path`).
- `reclaimPolicy` — what happens to a *dynamically* provisioned PV when its claim is deleted: `Delete` (default) or `Retain`. (`Recycle` is deprecated.)
- `volumeBindingMode` — `Immediate` binds/provisions as soon as the PVC is created; `WaitForFirstConsumer` waits until a pod schedules, so the volume lands on the correct node (essential for topology-constrained `local`/zonal disks).
- `parameters` — driver-specific (e.g. `type`, `fsType`); `allowVolumeExpansion: true` lets bound PVCs grow.
- `mountOptions`, `allowedTopologies` for finer control.

**Gotchas**
- `reclaimPolicy` and `volumeBindingMode` are **immutable** after creation — delete and recreate to change them.
- StorageClass is a *cluster-scoped* object (no namespace).
- `storageClassName: ""` on a PVC *disables* dynamic provisioning; **unset** means use the default class. These are not the same thing.

This kind cluster ships the `rancher.io/local-path` provisioner, which creates hostPath-backed volumes on demand.
questions.prompt:
Create a StorageClass named `fast-local` with provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`, `reclaimPolicy: Delete`, and `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`.

Target: `kubectl get sc fast-local` shows the class with that provisioner and binding mode.
questions.hint: Write a StorageClass manifest (apiVersion `storage.k8s.io/v1`) with the three fields, then `kubectl apply -f`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-local
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
YAML

verification.description: StorageClass fast-local exists with correct provisioner and binding mode

questions.title: PersistentVolume (hostPath)
questions.teach:
A **PersistentVolume (PV)** is a cluster-scoped piece of storage, provisioned by an admin (**static**) or by a StorageClass (**dynamic**).

**Key fields**
- `capacity.storage` — the size the PV offers.
- `accessModes` — `ReadWriteOnce` (RWO, one *node* r/w), `ReadOnlyMany` (ROX), `ReadWriteMany` (RWX, many nodes), `ReadWriteOncePod` (RWOP, exactly one pod).
- `persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy` — `Retain` / `Delete` (`Recycle` deprecated).
- `storageClassName` — ties the PV to a class; a PVC must match it to bind.
- A backing **source**, exactly one of: `hostPath` (single-node dev), `local` (node-pinned, needs `nodeAffinity`), `nfs`, `csi`, `emptyDir` is *not* a PV (pod-scoped, with `medium: Memory` and `sizeLimit` options).

**Gotchas**
- PV ↔ PVC bind **1:1**; a bound PV is exclusive to that claim.
- To bind, the PV capacity must **satisfy (be ≥)** the PVC request, and `accessModes` + `storageClassName` must match.
- `accessModes` describes capability, not enforcement; RWO is per-*node*, not per-pod (that's RWOP).
- `local` volumes require node affinity and only work with `WaitForFirstConsumer`; `hostPath` is single-node only.

Static PVs are how you pre-provision storage that a claim will later bind to.
questions.prompt:
Create a PersistentVolume named `pv-data` with capacity `1Gi`, accessModes `ReadWriteOnce`, `hostPath` at `/mnt/data`, and `storageClassName: fast-local`.

Target: `kubectl get pv pv-data` shows a 1Gi RWO volume.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-data
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-local
  hostPath:
    path: /mnt/data
YAML

verification.description: PV pv-data exists with 1Gi capacity and ReadWriteOnce access mode

questions.title: PersistentVolumeClaim (static bind)
questions.teach:
A **PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC)** is a *namespaced* request for storage.

**How binding happens**
- **Dynamic**: the PVC names a StorageClass (or uses the default) and the provisioner creates a PV on demand.
- **Static, automatic match**: the controller finds any existing PV matching the requested `resources.requests.storage`, `accessModes`, and `storageClassName`.
- **Static, explicit**: set `spec.volumeName` to a specific PV's name to force that bind (what this step does).
- **Selector**: `spec.selector` with `matchLabels` can narrow which PVs are eligible.

**Gotchas**
- A PVC's request must be **≤** the PV capacity; `accessModes` and `storageClassName` must match or the PVC stays **`Pending`**.
- `storageClassName: ""` disables dynamic provisioning (bind only to a pre-made PV); **omitting** it uses the default class.
- Binding is 1:1 and the PVC is sticky — once `Bound` it keeps that PV.
- Most spec fields (size, accessModes, class) are **immutable** after creation; only growing `resources.requests.storage` is allowed, and only if the class has `allowVolumeExpansion: true`.
- A PVC still in use by a pod won't fully delete (PVC protection finalizer).

Once bound, both the PVC and PV show status `Bound`.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `storage-learn`, create a PVC named `pvc-data` requesting `1Gi`, accessModes `ReadWriteOnce`, `storageClassName: fast-local`, bound explicitly to PV `pv-data` via `volumeName`.

Target: `kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc pvc-data` shows status `Bound` to `pv-data`.
questions.hint: PVC manifest with `spec.volumeName: pv-data` plus matching `storageClassName`, `accessModes`, and `resources.requests.storage: 1Gi`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-data
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: fast-local
  volumeName: pv-data
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
YAML
kubectl -n storage-learn get pvc pvc-data

verification.description: PVC pvc-data is Bound to pv-data

questions.title: Mount the PVC in a pod
questions.teach:
Storage is only useful once a pod consumes it. A pod references a PVC under `spec.volumes[].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName`, then mounts that volume into a container with `volumeMounts[].mountPath`.

**Volume-mount options**
- `readOnly: true` on either the volume reference or the `volumeMount`.
- `subPath` mounts a single file/subdirectory from the volume (handy to avoid clobbering a directory) — but `subPath` mounts do **not** receive later updates for ConfigMap/Secret-backed volumes.
- A PVC used by a pod must be in the **same namespace** as the pod (PVCs are namespaced; PVs are not).
- With `WaitForFirstConsumer`, the PV/PVC only binds once this pod is scheduled — so a `Pending` pod can keep a PVC `Pending` too.

**Gotchas**
- If the PVC is `Pending` or missing, the pod stays `Pending` (`FailedScheduling` / `unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims`) — it never reaches `Running`.
- An RWO volume can only be mounted by pods on **one node**; scheduling a second pod elsewhere blocks it.
- Permissions: use pod-level `securityContext.fsGroup` to let a non-root container write to the mounted volume.

Use the `busybox:1.36` image with a long-running command (`sleep 3600`) so the pod stays `Running` while the volume is mounted.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `storage-learn`, create a pod named `app` running `busybox:1.36` (command `sleep 3600`) that mounts PVC `pvc-data` at `/data`.

Target: pod `app` reaches `Running` with the PVC mounted at `/data`.
questions.hint: Pod manifest: `spec.volumes[0].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName: pvc-data`, and in the container `volumeMounts[0].mountPath: /data`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: app
  namespace: storage-learn
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: data
      mountPath: /data
  volumes:
  - name: data
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: pvc-data
YAML
kubectl -n storage-learn wait --for=condition=Ready pod/app --timeout=60s

verification.description: pod app is Running with pvc-data mounted at /data

questions.title: Default StorageClass
questions.teach:
When a PVC **omits** `storageClassName`, Kubernetes uses the cluster's **default StorageClass**. A class becomes default via the annotation `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"`.

**Ways to set/clear it**
- `kubectl patch storageclass <name> -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}'`.
- To *unset*, patch the same annotation to `"false"`.
- `kubectl annotate sc <name> storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true --overwrite` works too.

**Gotchas**
- Only **one** class should be default. If two are default, the newest-created one wins and the admission plugin is ambiguous — clear the extras.
- The annotation value must be the **string** `"true"` (quoted), not a bare boolean.
- Empty string vs unset: a PVC with `storageClassName: ""` deliberately **opts out** of the default and only binds to a pre-provisioned PV; **omitting** the field is what triggers the default.
- Since v1.28 the **Retroactive Default StorageClass** behavior means a PVC created with an *unset* `storageClassName` while no default exists stays pending and is assigned the default *retroactively* once one is created. A PVC that opted out with `storageClassName: ""` is never touched, and an already-**bound** PVC is never rebound.
- An older deprecated annotation `volume.beta.kubernetes.io/storage-class` exists — prefer the GA one above.

`kubectl get sc` flags the default with `(default)` next to its name.
questions.prompt:
Mark the StorageClass `fast-local` as the cluster default via the `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` annotation.

Target: `kubectl get sc` shows `fast-local (default)`.
questions.solution:
kubectl patch storageclass fast-local -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}'
kubectl get sc
